text:
Maya (oncall_infra): :rotating_light: Alerts firing for ap-northeast1: control plane and node health flapping, >90% pods in CrashLoopBackOff / 503s from inference API. PagerDuty triggered.
OpsBot: Incident created: INC-2026-2473 - ap-northeast1 - possible network partition (auto-detected by heartbeat gap).
Maya (oncall_infra): Observability: control-plane heartbeat gap at 1765207802, kube-apiserver errors 'connection refused' from most kubelets. Latency spike at the edge LB too.
Kevin (sre): Copy. Can someone run a quick `kubectl get nodes` against the ap-northeast cluster? I suspect node-networking state.
Jen (platform): Running now from bastion. Output:
```
$ kubectl --context=ap-northeast1 get nodes -o wide
NAME                       STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP      
node-1                     NotReady   <none>   120d  v1.27.3   10.128.5.12
node-2                     NotReady   <none>   98d   v1.27.3   10.128.5.13
node-3                     NotReady   <none>   45d   v1.27.3   10.128.5.14
```
Jen (platform): kubelet logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts to the control-plane, and coredns failing to reach 169.254.169.254 for metadata.
Carlos (netops): I see provider-side networking incidents for ap-northeast1 region — internal SDN reported packet loss between hypervisors starting ~1765207600. I'm opening ticket with provider (TKT-99321).
Kevin (sre): Ok, immediate triage: 1) Shift traffic away from ap-northeast1 to fallback regions (us-east1 primary standby) 2) Prevent autoscaler from creating new pods in ap-northeast until patch 3) Drain any stateful GPU workloads gracefully.
Maya (oncall_infra): I'm starting traffic-shift playbook now. Note: this will increase cross-region egress and GPU spot eviction risk for burst capacity. PD and infra costs will spike; will notify finance if we exceed commit.
InfraCI: Playbook step executed: `routemanager set-weight inference-router ap-northeast1 0 && routemanager set-weight inference-router us-east1 1` — change pushed at 1765207950.
Kevin (sre): Confirming failover: synthetic checks to us-east1 are green, global LB now returning us-east1 backends.
Jen (platform): Started draining GPU nodes in ap-northeast1. Command snippet: `for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o name); do kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300; done`
Carlos (netops): Provider update: "Investigating internal routing issue affecting ap-northeast1. Some customers experience control-plane API errors." ETA unknown.
Maya (oncall_infra): Notifying comms status page and support triage. Draft status update: "We have detected a network partition in ap-northeast1 impacting inference endpoints. Traffic has been shifted to us-east1; customers may see elevated latency. Working with provider and continuing mitigation."
Kevin (sre): Quick checks: - Ensure KV cache snapshotting in ap-northeast completed before shutting down (to avoid serving regressions). Jen, can you confirm snapshot success?
Jen (platform): KV snapshots started at 1765208020, progress logs show 82% for prefix caches, will complete ~1765208200.
Maya (oncall_infra): If provider can't restore within 30m, we escalate to SE and ask for live network debug. Also prepare Dedicated customers for potential long tail failovers and cost adjustments.
InfraCI: Added automation to pause non-critical batch GPU cronjobs in all regions to free capacity: `cron-manager pause --label=batch-gpu` at 1765208105.
Carlos (netops): Suggestion: open a BGP-level reroute with provider if internal SDN fix not arriving — will coordinate with provider lead.
Kevin (sre): Agree. Next updates in 10 minutes or when KV snapshots finish. Everyone keep replies short — ops channel is noisy. :thumbsup:
